Use this guide to adjust figures after running the [Standard demonstration](demonstration-standard.html). It reuses that study's matrices, metadata and fitted results. For data preparation, complete code, figures and interpretation, follow the study itself.

<div class="microfun-table-caption">Table 1. Community-level plotting choices</div>

| Plot | Useful controls | Study example |
|---|---|---|
| `pathway_pca()` | Feature subset and group `colors`. | [KO and KEGG PCA](demonstration-standard.html#compare-overall-functional-profiles). |
| `pathway_heatmap()` | Displayed features, `font_size`, `show_row_names`, `show_legend`, group `colors`. | [Selected-feature heatmaps](demonstration-standard.html#inspect-selected-features-across-samples). |
| `pathway_errorbar()` | `select`, `p_values_threshold`, `order`, `x_lab`, `p_value_bar`. | [Group abundance summaries](demonstration-standard.html#examine-group-abundance-summaries). |

## PCA colours and feature selection

The matrix rows are features and its columns are samples. Keep metadata aligned by sample identifier. Remove constant rows before scaled PCA, then supply one colour for each group in factor-level order.

```r
pathway_variance <- apply(kegg_abundance, 1, stats::var)
p_pca <- pathway_pca(
  kegg_abundance[is.finite(pathway_variance) & pathway_variance > 0, , drop = FALSE],
  meta, group = "group", colors = c("#B4CBE0", "#F5BB7C")
)
```

See the [Standard PCA](demonstration-standard.html#pca-at-kegg-pathway-level) for the resulting study view. Use the complete feature matrix for an overview, or a defined subset when you want to explore specific functions.

## Heatmap feature selection and labels

Choose the displayed features explicitly. `kegg_features` is the list used in the Standard study; the following example narrows it to ten pathways. Rows are standardized within the plotting function.

```r
selected_pathways <- head(kegg_features, 10L)
p_heatmap <- pathway_heatmap(
  kegg_abundance[selected_pathways, , drop = FALSE], meta,
  group = "group", colors = c("#B4CBE0", "#F5BB7C"),
  font_size = 9, show_row_names = TRUE, show_legend = TRUE
)
```

See the [Standard heatmaps](demonstration-standard.html#heatmap-of-selected-kegg-pathways) for the full displayed selection and interpretation. Smaller selections make individual labels easier to read.

## Error-bar selection and annotations

Use the study's `daa_kegg` result table. `select` controls the displayed IDs and `p_values_threshold` controls the significance filter. Keep the full abundance matrix as input so sample normalization precedes feature selection. Use `p_value_bar = TRUE` to display adjusted p-values in scientific notation; the CSV tables retain their numeric values.

```r
sample_groups <- factor(
  meta$group[match(colnames(kegg_abundance), meta$sample_name)],
  levels = c(reference, target)
)
p_errorbar <- pathway_errorbar(
  abundance = kegg_abundance, daa_results_df = daa_kegg,
  Group = sample_groups, select = selected_pathways,
  p_values_threshold = 0.05, order = "p_values",
  ko_to_kegg = FALSE, x_lab = "pathway_name", p_value_bar = TRUE
)
```

Use `x_lab = "description"` with the annotated KO results and `x_lab = "pathway_name"` with KEGG pathway results. See [Standard error bars](demonstration-standard.html#error-bar-plot-at-kegg-pathway-level) for the study output.

## Export a changed figure

```r
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(out, "selected_pathways_heatmap.pdf"), p_heatmap,
                width = 11, height = 6)
```

Use [Export and redraw](plot-export.html) for Sankey and Chord formats, and the [function reference](../reference/index.html) for complete argument lists.
